sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Bourbon County
sections.html:
Your bill comes from a division of labor inside the Paris courthouse building. Room 15 houses the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), who decides what the property is worth. Room 104 houses the Sheriff's Office, which prints the bills and receives payment.

The PVA's number is (859) 987-2152, extension 217, and the sheriff's number is (859) 987-2130. Both keep weekday hours from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The sheriff closes on holidays, including Good Friday, Memorial Day and Thanksgiving, so plan around those days if you are paying in person.

Farmland rolls out around Paris, and Millersburg and North Middletown are the other small towns. About 20,243 people live here in 9,399 housing units. A typical home is worth $229,300, and owners occupy 63.7% of them. Few people move: 94.9% stayed in the same house over the past year, which keeps listings scarce. Builders took out 109 permits in 2025.

If you own acreage, ask the PVA in Room 15 for the parcel record and compare it with a recent local sale before you accept the assessed figure as right.

The Sheriff's Office collects from November 1 through April 15. The earlier you pay, the less you owe. A U.S. postmark counts as the date of payment.

Delinquent notices are mailed February 1. After April 15 each unpaid bill is handed to the County Clerk, and significant extra fees follow. Selling in spring? Ask where your bill is now.

sections.h2: How to pay a Bourbon County tax bill
sections.html:
You can walk in at 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or mail a check to the same address. The bill is a postcard sent to the homeowner. When a lender pays from escrow, check with the lender about whether it also needs a copy.

  • Cash, cashier's checks, money orders, and personal or business checks from U.S. banks all work.
  • Credit and debit cards work at the counter only, and a 3.5% fee comes with them.
  • The office turns away third party checks and foreign funds.
  • If a check bounces you pay $50, and the bill stays unpaid.

sections.h2: What to bring to the Sheriff's Office
sections.html:
Carry the postcard or your parcel details, and a form of payment from the list above. Checks are payable to the Bourbon County Sheriff's Office. Payment by phone or online is not offered, so you will need either a visit or a stamp.

  • A mailed check is dated by its postmark, so drop it in the mail early in November if you want the discount.
  • Make sure the check comes from a U.S. bank and carries your own name, not someone else's.
  • Also expect closures on Martin Luther King Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Christmas and New Year's, in addition to the holidays listed above.

sections.h2: Can I dispute a Bourbon County assessment?
sections.html:
Yes. The value is set as of January 1, and the first step needs no paperwork: ask the PVA or a deputy to meet with you.

KRS 133.120 sets out the process. Book your conference in May, while the county's inspection window is open. It lasts two weeks, though the state may extend it. If the talk goes nowhere, mail the County Clerk a letter stating why you disagree and what you think the house is worth. That letter reaches the board of assessment appeals through the clerk, and it must arrive one workday after the window closes. Show up at the hearing with nearby sales, an appraisal or a repair estimate from a contractor.

Keep paying while you appeal. Base the payment on the value you claim, and expect to owe the difference plus interest if the board decides on more. Going straight past the county board also shuts you out of the state-level Board of Tax Appeals.

The exemption here is the one set by the state, and you qualify by turning 65 or by being classed as totally disabled. For 2025 and 2026 the deduction is $49,100, and the state resets the figure every two years.

File the application at the PVA's desk. The deduction is subtracted from the assessed value first, and tax is figured on what is left. Disability claims must be renewed each year, with two exceptions: owners with a service-connected disability, and owners that Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently disabled. Check with the PVA to learn which deduction your current bill reflects.

Timing changes the total a lot. November earns the 2% discount, December costs the plain amount, January adds 5%, and the 21% penalty period covers February 1 through April 15. Between the November rate and the last collection day, the gap is more than a quarter of the bill.

Once the clerk has the bill, the clerk's own fees get added, so the payoff is the figure quoted the day you pay. Sellers with an old unpaid year should phone the clerk for it before choosing a closing date.

sections.h2: The Bourbon County tax year in order
sections.html:
The same calendar repeats every year.

  • January 1: the assessment date. The PVA values the property as it stands that day.
  • May: the two-week inspection window, when you can sit down with the PVA or a deputy.
  • The workday after the window closes: your written appeal reaches the County Clerk.
  • November 1: the Sheriff's Office starts collecting, and the 2% discount runs through November 30.
  • February 1: delinquent notices are mailed.
  • April 15: collection ends at the sheriff's desk, and unpaid bills go to the clerk.

If you list in spring, find out where your bill sits in that sequence. Title companies ask the same thing, and a bill already at the clerk takes longer to clear.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when you sell?
sections.html:
Tax left unpaid attaches to the house, though the debt itself is owed by the person who held title on January 1. Your closing agent checks that the bill is current. The buyer's lender or title company will also want the deed and any lien releases in hand, and all of that paper comes out of offices at 301 Main Street.

  • Call the sheriff to learn whether this year's bill is paid, and which period it falls in.
  • Write the buyer's mailing address on the deed's tax-bill line, so the next postcard reaches them.
  • Settle with the buyer how this year's tax will be divided.
  • An older unpaid year is a clerk matter, so the clerk gives that payoff.

Owners here spend about $1,424 a month with a mortgage and $466 without one, and the tax bill is a slice of that. A cash buyer skips the lender's escrow questions, but the tax check at title stays the same.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to avoid a penalty on a Bourbon County bill?
faqs.a: Pay by December 31 and you owe only the face amount. The 2% discount stops after November 30, and the 5% penalty starts January 1.

faqs.q: Where can I hand over a Bourbon County tax payment?
faqs.a: Go to the Sheriff's Office at 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or send it by mail. Cards are taken in person only, and the fee is 3.5%.

faqs.q: What happens to a Bourbon County bill unpaid after April 15?
faqs.a: It moves from the sheriff to the County Clerk, with significant added fees. Ask the clerk what the payoff is.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Bourbon County property assessment?
faqs.a: Ask the PVA for a conference in May. If you do not settle there, file a written petition with the County Clerk one workday after the inspection window ends.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for the Bourbon County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Anyone 65 or older, and anyone classed as totally disabled, can apply through the PVA. The deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026.
